title: client-directed schema prefetch shim to reduce on-request negotiation and stabilize streaming
author: Aisha K. Patel
release_notes: Adds an opt-in client-directed schema prefetch header to reduce request-time negotiation and improve streaming stability; includes backward-compat shim for clients that do not opt in. No breaking changes by default.
description: Motivation: We see a class of user-reported flakiness and tail-latency regressions on the OpenAI-compat proxy when clients repeatedly negotiate schema versions on first call, especially for streaming + tool-calling flows. Negotiation involves schema validation and dynamic adapter selection which adds jitter to the streaming handshake and occasionally triggers incompatible fallback paths. This PR introduces a lightweight, opt-in client-directed schema prefetch shim that lets clients advertise and pre-warm their preferred request/response schema ahead of invocation, reducing per-request negotiation work and stabilizing streaming handoffs. The change also includes a conservative backward-compatibility path: if a client does not send the new header we fall back to the existing negotiation logic. Checklist: - [x] Add new header handler: X-Redwood-Prefer-Schema-Prefetch (values: schema:v2, schema:v1, auto) - [x] Server-side prefetch cache keyed by client_id (TTL 24h) with eviction heuristics - [x] Proxy change: avoid layered validation during streaming handshake when prefetch hits - [x] SDK opt-in helpers to set the header (TypeScript and Python) - [x] Validation tests and streaming e2e scenario that previously flaked - [x] Backward-compat shim to ensure older clients still negotiate normally - [x] Documentation and migration notes in openai-compat README Implementation notes: The header is advisory. When present and accepted the proxy records the preferred schema on the client prefetch cache and skips the heavier negotiation path for subsequent requests until TTL expiry. We added a fast-path in the streaming handshake that trusts the cached mapping and only performs a lightweight version check; if any validation mismatch occurs the proxy falls back to the full negotiation flow and emits a metric (openai.compat.prefetch.miss). To keep risk low the feature is gated behind an opt-in header and the proxy emits informational logs and metrics on acceptance, eviction, and mismatch. Testing: Unit tests cover header parsing, cache behavior, and mismatch fallbacks. We exercised streaming tool-calls using the flaky integration harness (see ENG-2399) and observed 45-65% reduction in handshake latency P95 across representative traces. A small load test confirmed no measurable regression in throughput with prefetch enabled. Security/compatibility: The prefetch cache respects tenant isolation. Prefetch values are validated against the server catalog; unrecognized values are rejected and logged. No sensitive data is stored. Rollout plan: - Stage 1: Merge behind a feature flag on the proxy, enable for internal clients only - Stage 2: Opt into TS/Python SDK helpers and experimental note in the public docs - Stage 3: Open beta for customer opt-in and monitor metrics for two weeks - Stage 4: Consider automatic suggestion by Redwood Optimize if stability gains are consistent Migration notes: Send X-Redwood-Prefer-Schema-Prefetch: schema:v2 to pre-warm v2 behavior. If you do not opt-in nothing changes. See release notes for more detail.

conversation: Diego Moreno (reviewer): The fast-path looks good but we need to be cautious about trusting cached schema with streaming where tool-calls can change mid-stream. Please ensure a fail-safe that re-runs full negotiation if the first token of structured output doesn't validate.

Aisha K. Patel (author): Good point — added a lightweight validation step that checks the first structured chunk and triggers a fallback negotiation if it fails. See handshake_stream.py delta. Also added a metric openai.compat.prefetch.invalid_first_chunk.
Ling Zhao (reviewer): Tests look solid. Please add a note about tenant isolation in the docs and ensure cache keys include region and tenant_id.
Aisha K. Patel (author): Done — cache now uses tenant_id+region as the key and the README notes tenant isolation.
